The 2023 comparatives on the statement of financial position and in note 14 (Debtors) and note 17 (Creditors) are labelled 'as restated', reflecting a netting of intercompany balances under a Multilateral Netting Deed. While note 14 briefly explains the mechanics of the offset, neither that note nor any other note discloses: (a) the nature of the prior period error (i.e. whether this is a correction of a misstatement or merely a reclassification, and why the original presentation was incorrect); (b) the amount of the correction for each financial statement line affected on a gross-to-net basis with clear quantification of the restatement impact; or (c) confirmation of which other lines, if any, were affected. FRS 102 Section 10 requires that when a prior period error is corrected, the entity discloses the nature of the error and the amount of the correction for each financial statement line item affected. This disclosure is absent, meaning users cannot assess the significance or propriety of the restatement. (confidence 0.82)

The company recognises a deferred tax asset of £41,970 at 31 December 2024, of which £41,306 (approximately 98%) relates to tax losses carried forward. The company reported an operating loss in 2024 and a significant decline in profitability. While the accounting policy correctly states that recognition of deferred tax assets is limited to the extent it is probable they will be recovered against future taxable profits, the notes provide no evidence or explanation to support the recoverability of this loss-related deferred tax asset — no forward-looking profit forecasts, no discussion of the basis for concluding recovery is probable, and no disclosure of the amount of unrecognised losses (if any). Given the loss-making position and difficult trading conditions described, the absence of any recoverability assessment or disclosure is a quality concern. (confidence 0.72)
